primary_warning.label: Commodities inflation impulse
primary_warning.why_it_matters: Commodity-driven inflation impulse pressures rates and discount-rate-sensitive assets.

sections.answer: Commodity prices are subtracting from inflation pressure (impulse -47.1, 100th percentile of the past year).
sections.caveat: Commodity impulse blends oil and crop momentum with breakeven confirmation; monthly food/oil pass-through varies.
sections.question: Are commodity prices adding to or subtracting from inflation pressure?
sections.support: Easing commodity prices reduce inflation pressure and rate-cut risk.
sections.why: A negative commodity impulse eases headline inflation pressure and supports disinflation.

primary_support.label: Credit spreads
primary_support.why_it_matters: Credit spreads confirm whether stress is spreading beyond equities into corporate funding markets.

sections.answer: The HY-IG OAS spread is roughly stable (-0.05 pp over 30 days at 1.98 pp); credit dispersion is not currently widening or tightening.
sections.caveat: OAS spreads are derived daily from ICE BofA indices via FRED; intraday credit moves not reflected.
sections.question: Is the HY-IG spread widening (early credit stress) or tightening (risk-on)?
sections.support: Steady credit dispersion is not amplifying cross-asset stress.
sections.why: Stable HY-IG dispersion describes a credit market without a directional impulse.

primary_support.label: Broad dollar
primary_support.message: The broad dollar backdrop is easing.
primary_support.why_it_matters: Dollar moves transmit global liquidity and risk-off pressure across asset classes.

sections.answer: The broad dollar is roughly stable (+0.48% over one month at 119.29); dollar pressure is not adding to global conditions in either direction.
sections.caveat: Broad dollar uses Fed's nominal trade-weighted index; FX series can be stale around holidays.
sections.question: Is the broad dollar tightening or easing global financial conditions?
sections.support: Stable dollar is not amplifying global financial-condition pressure.
sections.why: A stable broad dollar describes a balanced FX channel for global liquidity.

primary_support.label: Growth breadth
primary_support.why_it_matters: Broad growth conditions set the strategic backdrop for risk assets and recession risk.

sections.answer: Growth breadth is mixed: 3 of 5 growth and labor inputs are constructive while others have softened.
sections.caveat: Breadth uses heuristic thresholds; release timing varies by indicator and some inputs may lag.
sections.question: Is broad-based growth firm, mixed, or softening across labor and production inputs?
sections.why: Mixed growth breadth describes an economy with both expansionary and contractionary pockets.

growth.title: Growth
growth.why_it_matters: Broad growth conditions set the strategic backdrop for risk assets and recession risk.

sections.answer: Housing activity is resilient despite elevated rates: starts and permits are rising over three months with the 30Y mortgage at 6.51%.
sections.caveat: Housing starts and permits are monthly; mortgage rate updates weekly. Series can move in opposite directions over short horizons.
sections.question: Is housing activity expanding or contracting given current mortgage rates?
sections.support: Resilient housing activity despite elevated rates suggests demand backstop.
sections.why: Housing turnover is holding up despite the most rate-sensitive sector facing high financing costs.

primary_warning.label: Inflation pressure
primary_warning.why_it_matters: Inflation trajectory drives Fed policy expectations and real-yield direction.

sections.answer: Core and headline inflation are aligned and rising (headline 3.9% YoY, core CPI 3.0% YoY, both firming).
sections.caveat: YoY changes are computed from monthly index levels; release timing differs across CPI, PCE, and PPI.
sections.question: Are core and headline inflation moving in the same direction or diverging?
sections.risk: Headline and core re-accelerating together complicates Fed easing expectations.
sections.why: Aligned reacceleration in headline and core describes a broad rebuild of inflation pressure.

inflation.title: Inflation
inflation.why_it_matters: Inflation trajectory drives Fed policy expectations and real-yield direction.

primary_support.label: Net liquidity
primary_support.why_it_matters: Net liquidity defines the funding backdrop for risk assets and dealer balance sheets.

sections.answer: Net liquidity is expanding (+$207B over four weeks to $5,907B); Fed balance sheet outpaces TGA and reverse repo drain.
sections.caveat: Net liquidity is a derived weekly proxy from Fed assets, TGA, and reverse repo — not a measure of funding-market stress.
sections.question: Is net liquidity expanding or contracting, and which Fed components are driving it?
sections.support: Expanding net liquidity supports risk-asset funding.
sections.why: Rising net liquidity loosens funding conditions across risk assets and credit.

liquidity.title: Liquidity
liquidity.why_it_matters: Net liquidity defines the funding backdrop for risk assets and dealer balance sheets.

primary_warning.label: 10Y real yields
primary_warning.message: Real yields are elevated and pressuring valuations.
primary_warning.why_it_matters: Higher real yields tighten financial conditions and weigh on valuation-sensitive assets.

sections.answer: The recent 10Y move (higher) is driven by real yields (+24 bps), not inflation expectations.
sections.caveat: Decomposition uses FRED TIPS and nominal yields; intraday moves not reflected.
sections.question: Is the recent 10Y move coming from real yields, breakevens, or curve shape?
sections.risk: Rising real yields compress equity valuations across all sectors.
sections.why: Real-yield-driven moves tighten financial conditions more directly than inflation-driven moves.

rates.title: Rates
rates.why_it_matters: Higher real yields tighten financial conditions and weigh on valuation-sensitive assets.

sections.answer: Real yield and dollar moves are within neutral thresholds over the short window; no dominant directional driver is evident.
sections.caveat: 20D window uses closing prices; intraday volatility and FX moves not captured.
sections.question: Are real yields and the dollar tightening or easing financial conditions together?
sections.support: Absence of a dominant tightening impulse leaves conditions in a holding pattern.
sections.why: Neutral short-window readings suggest the regime is consolidating rather than trending.

regime_map.title: Regime map
regime_map.why_it_matters: The regime quadrant blends rates, dollar and risk inputs.

sections.answer: Asset-manager S&P 500 net positioning is within a neutral range at the 73th percentile of the past year (+48.6% OI).
sections.caveat: CFTC data is weekly and delayed by several days; short-term positioning shifts are not captured. NAAIM is a candidate source and may be absent.
sections.question: Is positioning crowded enough to amplify downside?
sections.support: Positioning is not stretched enough to generate a crowding-driven unwind.
sections.why: Neutral positioning does not add amplification pressure in either direction.
